figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Discovery and identification of new cyclopentachromones. (a) Chemical structures of representative cyclopentachromones. (b)
Schematic architectures of the engineered cytosine base editor hA3AY130F and the tRNA-gRNA array for multiple sgRNA generation. (c) Compared
metabolic profile of (i) WT and (ii) QCCS. (d) Chemical structures of C-3 epimers isochromosulfines (1 and 2) and emodin derivatives (3 and 4)
found in QCCS. DA reaction, Diels−Alder reaction.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthetic investigation of isochromosulfines. (a) The putative isc gene cluster from P. citrinum ATCC 9849. (b) HPLC analysis (UV
254 nm) of metabolic profiles of QCCS and Isc deletion mutants. (i) QCCS, (ii) ΔiscC, (iii) ΔiscN, (iv) ΔiscM, (v) ΔiscG, (vi) ΔiscP, (vii) ΔiscK,
(viii) ΔiscF, (ix) ΔiscH, (x) ΔiscL, and (xi) ΔiscR. (c) Proposed biosynthetic pathway of ISCs.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Characterization of IscL. (a) LC-MS analysis of metabolites from feeding experiments of IscL. Feeding of 10 to A. nidulans with (i) IscL
and (ii) empty vector; (b) HPLC analysis of in vitro assays of IscL (UV 254 nm). (i) Standard 1, (ii) Standard 2, 50 μL aliquot containing 50 mM
Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 0.1 mM 10, 0.5 mM NADPH, and 0.25 mM FAD with (iii) boiled IscL, (iv) 0.5 mM 12 and IscL, or (v) with 10 μM IscL, (vi)
50 μL aliquot contains 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 0.1 mM 16, and 0.5 mM 12. All reactions were incubated at 30 °C for 30 min. *represents the
unknown impurities incorporated in commercial product 12. (c) Isotopic labeling experiments. Mass spectra of 16 produced by IscL (i) without or
(ii) with 18O2. Mass spectra of 1 produced by the incubation of 16 and 12 in (iii) H2O or (iv) in D2O. (d) Ring contraction pathway of ISCs
catalyzed by IscL and proposed mechanism of spontaneous C−S bond formation.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Divergent pathways mediated by IscL homologues. (a) In vitro assays of CcxS, IscL and chimeric proteins produced by protein grafting.
50 μL aliquot containing 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 0.1 mM 10, 0.5 mM NADPH, and 0.25 mM FAD (i) without enzymes, (ii) with10 μM CcxS,
(iii) with 10 μM IscL, (iv-ix) with 10 μM chimeric proteins of IscL with the replacement of Segment I, Segment II, Segment III, Segment IV,
Segment V, and Segment VI, respectively. (b) Partial protein sequences of IscL homologues and in vitro assays of (ii) IscL F230Y mutant, and
other homologues including (iii) TaiL, (v) MofL, and (vi) LesL with the same condition mentioned above. (c) Predicted protein structure of IscL
by AlphaFold3 and Segments I, II, III, IV, V, and VI were colored with purple, beige, blue, red, yellow, and green, respectively (the details of the
protein grafting were shown in Figure S13). (d) Overlay of substrate-binding site view of IscL-FAD-10 (10 carbons colored in blue, residue carbons
colored in green, and FAD carbons colored in yellow). (e) Two distinct pathways mediated by IscL and CcxS and proposed enzymatic mechanism.
